entries.note: Picture-in-picture geometry is in pip.rs: the shrunken picture's size, the corner it rests in, and where a dragged picture snaps. Built 2026-10-17: shell/pip.rs draw_window fills the placed window above the windows and blits a frame already scaled to it, clipped to the surface (tests shell::pip::tests). Built 2026-10-17: Shell holds the window in shell/pip.rs Floating (controller, corner, aspect) and Shell::draw paints it over the screen between the menu bar and the dock while it is starting or active (Shell::pip_start, pip_stop; tests shell::pip::tests). Built 2026-10-17: the pip service (shell/services/picture_in_picture.rs) takes a player's possible, start and stop calls and delivers the delegate events as pip.will_start, pip.did_start, pip.will_stop and pip.did_stop (tests services::picture_in_picture::tests). Not built: the Music and Preview apps do not call the service yet, and frames are not scaled (the placeholder is drawn). Built 2026-10-17: the SDK client springboard/sdk/src/picture_in_picture.rs sends possible, start and stop to the pip service (set_possible, start, stop; tests picture_in_picture::tests). Still open: no player app calls the client yet.

entries.name: PackageUIKit
entries.note: Build the package install interface: a per-package progress sheet and a confirmation before scripts run. backup_page.rs notes that pacman reports no progress to the shell, so the progress needs a pacman hook or a log reader first. Built 2026-10-17: pacman_progress reads the steps of the latest transaction from the pacman log and gives a fraction for a progress bar (tests pacman_progress::tests). Built 2026-10-17: pacman_progress::progress gives the sheet's fraction against the packages it listed, and confirmation_needed says an install waits for the person before pacman runs its scripts (tests pacman_progress::tests). Built 2026-10-17: the install sheet (shell/package_install_sheet.rs) asks before the install runs, shows the install's progress from the pacman log, and needs the person's Install (tests package_install_sheet::tests).
entries.ready_note: Host tests for the shell path: opening a package archive in Files (workspace OpenFile) or a bifrost-package: store link opens the install sheet, nothing runs until Install is pressed (Return never installs), the install runs on a worker through privd (package.install_file, package.install_repo) with the progress read from the pacman log since the start, and the sheet shows the result with Done. privd refuses bad paths and names before pacman runs. entries.name: PacketParser
entries.note: Packet parsing library. Built 2026-10-17: core/src/packet_parser.rs reads Ethernet (with VLAN tags), ARP, IPv4 (checksum checked), IPv6 (extension headers skipped), TCP, UDP and ICMP into a Packet, gives a one-line summary, and reads classic pcap capture files (either byte order, micro and nanosecond stamps, Ethernet, raw IP and Linux cooked links) that tcpdump writes. Pure, tested (packet_parser::tests). No UI reads it yet.
entries.ready_note: The parser is pure and covered by host tests that build frames byte by byte: layers, checksum, VLAN, IPv6 extension headers, fragments, malformed and cut-short data, and capture files in all four magic variants. Capture itself is tcpdump (runtime-packages.txt); no app shows the parsed packets yet.

Not the reference's panic file format, which is XNU specific.
entries.ready_note: Kernel panic dumps on Linux live in pstore. pstore.rs recognises the panic and oops dumps (dmesg-* records) that survive a reboot, the boot supervisor reports and removes them, and the Console Kernel Reports view lists each record with its text and the previous boot's kernel warnings.

entries.name: PlatformSSO

entries.name: PlatformSSOCore
entries.note: Bundle com.apple.PlatformSSOCore is the core of the enterprise Platform SSO extension, which depends on the directory enrolment and device management that BifrOSt does not run.

entries.name: PlatformSSOCoreUI

entries.name: PlatformSSOUI

entries.name: PlugInKitDaemon
entries.note: extension_process.rs keeps the process table, one process per extension and host key, and its connections are in memory only. The reference daemon's persisted enablement state is not modelled.
entries.ready_note: Process table with one process per extension and host key (extension_process.rs). Enablement state is in memory only.

entries.name: PnROnDeviceFramework
entries.note: n/a: the on-device half of a server-assisted Apple ranking/ML service (the bundle holds only an Info.plist: no resources, no XPC service, and nothing else in the reference index links it). BifrOSt has no server-assisted services and ships no Apple ML model packs.

entries.name: PodcastServices
entries.note: Bundle com.apple.podcasts.PodcastServices is the vendor's podcast subscription and sync service; BifrOSt reads feeds directly in springboard/apps/podcasts-desktop/src/refresh.rs.

entries.name: PodcastsFoundation
entries.note: Feed parsing is in feed.rs and the podcast model in podcasts.rs. The reference's store catalogue and cloud sync are not part of BifrOSt.
entries.ready_note: Feed parsing in the Podcasts app (feed.rs, 13 tests). The store catalogue and cloud sync are not part of BifrOSt.

entries.name: PodcastsKit

entries.ready_note: Podcast library in podcasts.rs; playback and chapters in media.rs and chapters.rs.

entries.name: PoirotAnalytics
entries.note: PoirotAnalytics is the reference's usage analytics client, which collects events for the vendor's analytics and experimentation service; BifrOSt runs no such service.

entries.name: PoirotBlocks
entries.note: PoirotBlocks is the query-block layer of the reference's analytics pipeline (the Poirot family, next to the Poirot experimentation extension in the image); it only serves the vendor's analytics service.

entries.name: PoirotSQLite
entries.note: PoirotSQLite is the local event store of the reference's Poirot analytics pipeline, which buffers usage events for the vendor's analytics service; BifrOSt has no such event pipeline.

entries.name: PoirotSchematizer
entries.note: PoirotSchematizer defines the event schemas of the reference's Poirot analytics pipeline for the vendor's analytics service, so it has no meaning for BifrOSt.

entries.name: PoirotUDFs
entries.note: PoirotUDFs holds the user-defined functions the reference's Poirot analytics queries call; it only serves the vendor's analytics pipeline.

entries.name: PommesRankingCore
entries.note: Bundle com.apple.metadata.PommesRankingCore ranks metadata results; search_ranking.rs ranks search results with rules, and the reference's learned ranking model is not built.
entries.ready_note: Result ranking for search is built locally: BM25 over title and text, recency, and local open counts (search_rank.rs), plus the index order (spotindex.rs). It is rule and usage based, learned only from this machine's own opens; the reference's trained model is deliberately not reproduced (no Apple model packs).

entries.name: Portrait
entries.note: Portrait lighting from a depth map is built (portrait_lighting::relight, a Lambert model of our own). The reference's bundled background photographs are Apple artwork and are not reproduced.
entries.ready_note: Portrait lighting from a depth map is built (portrait_lighting::relight, a Lambert model of our own). The reference's bundled background photographs are Apple artwork and are not reproduced.

entries.ready_note: Core of the portrait effect: depth-map relighting is implemented in portrait_lighting.rs and tested.

entries.name: PostSiriEngagement
entries.note: private framework, owner Intents; from SDK matrix siri-kit.json
entries.ready_note: Apps declare [[intent]] tables in manifest.toml and serve them on their control socket. Search and the Shortcuts action library list and run an installed app's shortcut intents (shell::intents::runnable_shortcuts). The assistant answers with intent cards that run only after the user confirms them, and reads answers aloud when Speak Answers is on. Voice recognition is not built: nothing turns speech into an intent request, so Siri's spoken requests are not covered.

entries.name: PowerExperience

entries.name: PowerLog
entries.note: Battery level history: the shell samples the battery every five minutes and charts 24 hours in Settings. The reference's on-device power-log telemetry database and its collectors are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Battery level history sampled every five minutes and charted for 24 hours (battery.rs), with power_sources in the SDK. No on-device power-log database.

entries.name: PowerUI
entries.note: Battery readout and time estimates in the shell and the Battery settings page. The reference's learned time-to-empty model is not shipped, so estimates come from the kernel's supply readings.
entries.ready_note: Battery readout and time estimates from kernel supply readings (power_supply.rs) and the Battery settings page. No learned time-to-empty model.

entries.name: PowerlogCore

entries.name: PowerlogDatabaseReader

entries.name: PowerlogLiteOperators

entries.name: PredictedContextAlgorithms

entries.ready_note: Print model (paper, orientation, page options), print panel plug-ins and CUPS submission. The reference printer-tool service and paper tables are not mirrored.

entries.note: n/a: library for Apple's Pro Display XDR hardware (reference modes, brightness, firmware). The bundle holds only Info.plist and version.plist. BifrOSt does not target Apple displays.

entries.note: n/a: iOS-only build of the Siri Suggestions blending layer; no counterpart on a desktop.

entries.name: ProactiveContextClient
entries.note: n/a: client of Apple's proactive daemon that reports device context (app, location, activity) to the Siri Suggestions engine. BifrOSt does not collect cross-app context for suggestions (privacy-first).

entries.name: ProactiveDaemonSupport
entries.note: n/a: plumbing of Apple's proactive/Siri Suggestions daemon, which BifrOSt does not mirror (it harvests content across apps and learns from it; see ProactiveHarvesting).

entries.name: ProactiveEventTracker

entries.name: ProtocolBuffer
entries.note: Built 2026-10-17: clean-room protocol buffer wire codec in springboard/core/src/protobuf.rs. Not built: schema compilation or generated message types; callers read fields by number.

Tests protobuf::tests.

entries.name: PrototypeTools
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal prototyping and tuning tool (live-tweakable prototype settings for Apple's own design builds). The index shows only a bare framework with an en.lproj; no user or app feature, nothing to mirror.

entries.name: QOSToolkit
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal quality-of-service test toolkit for the network stack (probes and reports for Apple's QoS marking and Wi-Fi/cellular service classes). Index: a bare framework with localized strings only; no user or app API. Linux handles QoS in the kernel (tc, DSCP via socket options) and BifrOSt exposes the Link Conditioner model in sdk/link_conditioner.rs.

entries.name: Quagga
entries.note: n/a: Apple ML model pack: Resources/Networks holds an espresso net (anmd-model.espresso.net/.shape), a compiled MIL model and a 4.4 MB weights .bin plus a metallib for Apple GPU inference. Trained Apple models are not mirrored; BifrOSt runs its own open models.

entries.name: QueryParser
entries.note: Parses search-panel text into filters that the shell search applies. Not covered: the reference generative query functions and free-form natural-language intent parsing.
entries.ready_note: Search-panel text is parsed into filters (parse_query in spotindex.rs, 23 tests). Natural-language intent parsing is not built.

entries.name: QueryUnderstanding
entries.note: Query parsing and matching for search: covered by the shared search query models; Apple's per-language ML query assets are not mirrored.

entries.name: RESync
entries.note: n/a: Apple cloud-account sync client (RE Sync keeps account-bound data in step across a user's Apple devices through Apple's servers). Index: a bare framework (stub symlinks and _CodeSignature only), referenced by no other bundle. BifrOSt syncs through its own record_sync/cloud_records on BifrOSt Cloud.

entries.name: RTBuddyCrashlogDecoder
entries.note: Decodes crash logs from real-time coprocessor firmware on the vendor system-on-chip; BifrOSt has no such coprocessor firmware to decode.

entries.name: RTCReporting
entries.note: Reports from the vendor real-time video and telephony calling stack; BifrOSt ships no calling stack to report on.

entries.name: RTTUI
entries.note: User interface for Real-Time Text (TTY) during calls; the reference index lists a TTY data model in the sibling utilities framework, and BifrOSt has no telephony or call text stack.

entries.name: RTTUtilities
entries.note: Real-Time Text (TTY) utilities: the reference index holds a TTY data model for calls, and BifrOSt has no telephony or call text stack.

entries.name: RapidResourceDelivery
entries.note: n/a: Apple CDN delivery of resources (downloads fast-track assets from Apple-hosted servers). Index: a bare framework with no resources. BifrOSt ships assets through its own packages and update channel (assetpack, background_download), not an Apple service.

entries.name: Rapport
entries.note: Pairs and trusts nearby vendor devices for cross-device features such as activity hand-off; BifrOSt has no vendor device trust to mirror.

entries.name: RapportUI
entries.note: Pairing dialogs for the device pairing framework (pairing storyboards in the reference index); BifrOSt has no such pairing.

entries.name: RealityCoreTextureImport
entries.note: Texture import for the 3D scene stack; the 3D scene row in data/realitykit.json is n/a because BifrOSt has no AR or 3D scene layer.

entries.name: RealityFusion
entries.note: Sensor and scene fusion for the 3D scene stack; the 3D scene row in data/realitykit.json is n/a because BifrOSt has no AR or 3D scene layer.

entries.name: RealityIO
entries.note: Asset I/O for 3D scenes; the 3D scene row in data/realitykit.json is n/a because BifrOSt has no AR or 3D scene layer.

entries.name: Recap
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal UI performance test framework (automated scroll and animation benchmarks run from Apple's test harness; its sibling RecapPerformanceTesting also ships an iOSSupport copy). Apple internal test tooling; BifrOSt benchmarks run through tools/bench.py.

entries.name: RecapPerformanceTesting
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal performance-testing harness (sibling of Recap, with an iOSSupport Catalyst copy). Index: Info.plist and version.plist only. Apple internal test tooling; BifrOSt benchmarks run through tools/bench.py.

entries.name: Recount
entries.note: Performance counter access and analysis through Linux perf (sdk/perf_counters.rs); Apple-silicon counter tables are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Reading hardware and software performance counters and measuring work between two points is perf_counters.rs (Linux perf stat, counters the machine lacks come back as None) and counter_sample.rs. The reference's Analysis JSON (bottleneck, characteristics, metrics) is keyed to Apple CPU counters and is not mirrored.

entries.name: RecoveryOS
entries.note: Rolls the installer-defined Btrfs root back after a bad update, from the recovery subvolume. Gap: there is no separate recovery operating system to boot into, and the shell Recovery button only writes a mark.
entries.ready_note: Rolls the installer-defined Btrfs root back after a bad update from the recovery subvolume. No separate recovery OS; the shell Recovery button only writes a mark.

entries.name: ReflectionInternal
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal Swift/Objective-C runtime reflection support (inspecting object layouts for Apple's tooling). Index: a bare framework. BifrOSt apps are Rust with no Objective-C or Swift runtime to reflect on.

entries.name: RegulatoryDomain
entries.note: Set the wireless regulatory domain from the region setting (for example iw reg set with the country code) and show it in Wi-Fi settings; nothing in springboard/netd sets a country code. Built 2026-10-17: regdomain parses iw reg get and sets the domain with iw reg set, refusing anything but a two-letter country code. Built 2026-10-17: netd starts net::regdomain::follow_region, which reads region from settings.ini every 5 seconds and applies the country at start and on each change; the Wi-Fi page shows Country or Region (tests regdomain::tests, shell::pages::tests). Not built: a live check on the lab machine.
entries.ready_note: The regulatory domain follows the region setting (netd applies it at start and on change) and the Wi-Fi page shows the country; host-tested only.

entries.name: RelativeMotion
entries.note: n/a: Apple hardware: relative motion between Apple devices and accessories (Tempest, UWB/IMU fusion for AirPods and nearby devices); the index shows a TempestDiagnosticExtension.appex diagnostic plug-in. No equivalent hardware or data source on Arch.

entries.name: ReminderKit
entries.note: Reminder lists, tags, alerts and due dates work in the reminders app on the shared calendar store. Not covered: a separate reminder database and cloud sync.
entries.ready_note: Reminder lists, tags, alerts and due dates on the shared calendar store. No separate reminder database or cloud sync.

entries.name: ReminderKitInternal
entries.note: Reminders data layer (lists, smart lists, subtasks, repeat, grocery categories, store) covered by the Reminders app; cloud sync and Apple's grocery model files are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: The reminder data layer is the Reminders app's own: lists, smart lists, subtasks, repeat rules, undoable deletion and grocery sections (model.rs, organize.rs, repeat.rs), quick-add parsing (quick.rs) and the atomic store (store.rs). The reference's CloudKit sync and its grocery ML factor files are not mirrored.

entries.name: ReminderKitUI
entries.note: The reminders app draws its lists, tags and detail views. Not covered: the reference reminder editor components.
entries.ready_note: The reminder list, detail editor (title, notes, URL, date, time, repeat, early alert, flag, priority, subtasks, location) and swipe actions are the Reminders app's own views (app.rs, view.rs, chrome.rs); tests drive them through the same touch and keyboard paths.

entries.name: RemindersAppIntents
entries.note: private framework, owner AppIntents; from SDK matrix app-intents.json The App Intents framework layer is ready (see the AppIntents row); this Apple app's own intents are not ported.
entries.ready_note: The Reminders app declares seven intents in its manifest (Add Reminder, Create List Item, Add Quick Reminder, Create List, Open List, Open Smart List, Search Reminders), runs them through perform_intent in main.rs (tests in app::actions_tests) and answers the scripting commands (scripting.rs); the shell lists and runs manifest intents (shell/intents.rs).

entries.name: RemindersIntentsFramework
entries.note: Reminder intents for voice assistants and automation; BifrOSt reminder intents are not wired, so no owner was verified.
entries.ready_note: The voice-and-typed-request side of Reminders (create a reminder or list, open a list, search) is the same manifest intents, resolved from typed or spoken parameters (intent_resolve.rs) and run by the shell on the app's control socket (shell/intents.rs); the app performs them in main.rs.

entries.name: RemindersUICore
entries.note: The reminders app draws its lists, tags and detail views. Not covered: the reference shared UI core components.
entries.ready_note: The shared UI pieces under the Reminders views (list rows with completion circle and subtask indent, date and time pickers, repeat and alert editors, smart-list grid) are the Reminders app's own drawing and input code (view.rs, chrome.rs, app.rs).

entries.name: RemoteCompositorServices
entries.note: n/a: visionOS Compositor Services: lets an app render immersive content that a remote host compositor shows on Apple Vision hardware (default.metallib 37 MB of Apple GPU shaders, localized prompt strings). Apple spatial hardware path; BifrOSt has its own window server and no headset.

entries.name: RemoteConfiguration

entries.name: RemoteCoreML
entries.note: n/a: Apple-device offload of Core ML inference (runs a model on a paired Apple device or Apple-hosted runtime). Index: a bare framework with Info.plist and version.plist only. BifrOSt runs models in-process through ml_runtime/core_ml and keeps inference local.

entries.name: RemoteHID
entries.note: n/a: Apple Continuity input forwarding (HID events from a nearby Apple device or accessory delivered over Apple's proprietary link, as in Universal Control and iPhone Mirroring). Index: bare framework, Info.plist only. BifrOSt handles local HID in hid_devices/hid_virtual and remote desktops over its screen-sharing app.

entries.name: RemoteManagement
entries.note: Declarative and MDM device management from a remote server; the Device Management row in data/device-management.json is n/a for BifrOSt, which has no MDM service.

entries.name: RemoteManagementModel
entries.note: Model of the vendor's MDM enrollment and managed settings, which only that vendor's enterprise server can issue (the same reason data/device-management.json is n/a). BifrOSt has no MDM client.

entries.name: RemoteManagementProtocol
entries.note: Command and check-in protocol between a managed device and the vendor's enterprise push service and MDM server; BifrOSt runs no such server and has no client for it.

entries.name: RemoteManagementStore
entries.note: Local store of enrollment state and managed profiles that exist only after enrolling in the vendor's device-management service, which BifrOSt does not offer.

entries.name: RemoteManagementUI
entries.note: Enrollment and management prompts for the vendor's MDM service; the reference index lists localized resources for it, and BifrOSt has no enrollment flow to show them in.

entries.name: RemotePairingDevice
entries.note: n/a: iOS/visionOS developer-device pairing (pairs a Mac with an iPhone, iPad or Apple TV for Xcode and CoreDevice, with a 6 MB code plus a Localizable.loctable of pairing prompts). Apple-only device tooling with no Linux or BifrOSt peer.

entries.name: RemoteServiceDiscovery
entries.note: n/a: Remote Service Discovery for Apple mobile devices: the RemoteXPC handshake that lists the services of a connected iPhone or iPad. Apple-only protocol with no open equivalent; index shows a bare framework.

entries.name: RemoteSoftwareUpdate
entries.note: The local update path is covered: the update agent checks, downloads and installs system packages, and the recovery guard gates base-system upgrades. Updates pushed by a managed-device server are not built, and the framework's exact role is inferred from its name.
entries.ready_note: Local update path: the updated agent checks, downloads and installs packages and the recovery guard gates base upgrades. Managed-device pushes are not built.

entries.name: RemoteTextInput
entries.note: Investigated 2026-10-14: the reference index holds only the bundle folders, no binary is extracted (the payload needs macOS to decode), and the name does not show its job; left os.
entries.ready_note: Text input between an app and the separate input-method process (client session, marked text, candidates, commit and cancel, and key routing to the provider) is imsession.rs and imroute.rs, with the shell-side bridge in shell/input_methods and fcitx_bridge.rs. Remote keyboards over Apple's Continuity link are not mirrored.

entries.name: RemoteUI

entries.name: RemoteXPC
entries.note: n/a: RemoteXPC: XPC carried over the network to Apple mobile devices (the transport under CoreDevice and Remote Service Discovery). Apple-only protocol; BifrOSt IPC is local sockets and its own control protocol. Index: bare framework.

entries.name: RenderBox
entries.note: Render engine covered by the display list, effect chain and bifrost-gpu pipeline/shader code; Apple's metallib shader archives are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: The GPU 2D/3D render engine behind view drawing is BifrOSt's own Vulkan stack: recorded display lists with damage and culling (display_list.rs), filter chains (effect_chain.rs) and the Metal-shaped bifrost-gpu pipelines and shaders. The reference's compiled shader archives (archive.metallib, default.metallib) are Apple GPU code and are not mirrored.

entries.name: ReplayKitMacHelper
entries.note: Remaining from data file replaykit (refreshed 2026-10-17): No screen video recording for apps, the shell or the MCP tools (screen streams deliver one frame per event, sdk screen_stream.rs, and nothing encodes a movie). | No SDK API for recording: no RPScreenRecorder equivalent in springboard/sdk/src/. | Microphone recording (springboard/src/media/capture.rs) is not reachable from app SDK code; it is used by Voice Memos only. | No app or system audio capture; audiod does not loop back output. | No clip export, preview or trim UI; the clip buffer model is in springboard/ui/src/clip_buffer.rs. | No live broadcast extension point or broadcast picker.
entries.ready_note: The helper only hosts ReplayKit's two macOS extension UIs: the broadcast activity picker and the video editor. Those jobs are broadcast.rs (service picker, ingest check, start, pause, resume and finish lifecycle, tests in ui/tests/parity_sdk-gaps-01.rs), clip_buffer.rs (the clip model) and media_trim.rs (trim). Actual screen video capture and encoding stays tracked on the ReplayKit row.

entries.name: Reveal
entries.note: Look Up popover: dictionary definition and quick search hits for the selected word (shell look_up_popover, bifrost_ui::look_up). The reference index lists only localized resources for this bundle.

BifrOSt shows it from the Services menu and Ctrl+Cmd+D: the content model and its rows are bifrost_ui::look_up over the local dictionary reader (stardict), and look_up_popover.rs measures, draws and hit tests it. entries.name: RunningBoard
entries.note: Focus, on-screen visibility and suspension of each app are modelled in the pure occlusion model, with a grace period before suspension. The model does not yet suspend processes or send memory-pressure events (task 008 is open), and there are no process assertions. Built 2026-10-17: memory pressure is parsed from /proc/pressure/memory and reported once per level change (core memory_pressure); suspend and resume map to SIGSTOP and SIGCONT (occlusion::signal_for). Built 2026-10-17: the shell feeds occlusion facts for each external app (background.rs Suspender: focus and whether a window is shown) and sends SIGSTOP after the grace period and SIGCONT on focus, only while the Suspend Background Apps switch (suspend_background, off by default) is on; turning it off resumes the stopped apps (tests shell::background::tests). Not built: covering is not known yet (a shown app is never stopped), audio playing in the background is not exempt, and apps are not told about memory pressure, which needs a protocol message. Built 2026-10-17: window covering is computed by is_covered (cuts the visible part of a window by each window above it; tests occlusion::tests); process assertions keep an app running (Event::Assertion). Still missing: the shell does not yet feed covering or assertions to the model, and memory-pressure events need a protocol message. Built 2026-10-17: covering is now fed by the shell (springboard/src/shell/mod.rs app_covered over the desktop stacking order, into background::Facts.covered); tests occlusion::tests and shell::background::tests::a_covered_app_is_stopped_after_the_grace_period. Still missing: apps cannot take process assertions over the protocol, and memory-pressure events are not sent to apps.
entries.ready_note: The main job, stopping and resuming apps by their run state (focus, shown, covered, after a grace period), is done: the pure model and the shell feed. Process assertions and memory-pressure messages to apps are open and need a protocol message.

entries.name: RunningBoardServices
entries.note: Built 2026-10-17: app run state (bifrost_core::occlusion) and, new this wave, process assertions an app takes over the runningboard system service (core process_assertion, shell services running_board, SDK running_board), fed to the Suspender. Launch-time limits live in the background service (30 s refresh, 10 min processing).
entries.ready_note: RunningBoard keeps app run state and process assertions. The run state (focus, on screen, covered, suspended) is bifrost_core::occlusion driven by shell::background::Suspender. Assertions are bifrost_core::process_assertion (reason, lapse limit of 60 s by default and 1 h at most, 8 per app), taken by apps over the runningboard service (bifrost_app::running_board) and read by the Suspender on every tick, so an app that holds one is not stopped and a quit app loses them. Time limits for background launches are the background service's refresh and processing limits. Not mirrored: assertion domains and per-process memory or CPU limits.
